questions.q: If \(L>M, M=N\) and \(D < M\), then which of the following relations will be false?
questions.solution:
Given:
\(L>M, M=N\) and \(D < M\).
Option 1) \(\mathrm{L}>$\mathrm{D} \rightarrow$\) True. (As \($\mathrm{L}$>$\mathrm{M}$\) and M D definitely holds.)
Option 2) \(M < L \rightarrow\) True. (\(L>M\) so the converse that is \(L>M\) definitely holds.)
Option 3) \(L>N → \) True. \((L>M, M=N\), this implies that \(L>N\).)
Option 4) \(N < D \rightarrow\) False. (\(M=N\) and \(D < M\), this implies that \(N>D\).)
Therefore, only the fourth option is false.
Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
questions.source: English and Logical Reasoning Prep Guide

questions.q: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right in the blanks below to balance the given equation. \(8 \_27 \_9 \_6 \_5=0\)
questions.solution: Given equation: 8 _ 27 _ 9 _ \(6 \_5=0\) Option 1) +, -, +, + Mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right: \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 8+27-9+6+5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 46-9=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 37=0 \end{aligned}\) Option 2),\(+, \div,-,-\) Mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right: \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 8+\underline{27 \div 9}-6-5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{8+3}-6-5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 11 \underline{-6-5}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{11-11}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 0=0 \end{aligned}\) Option 3),\(- ,\div,+,+\) Mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right: \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 8-\underline{27 \div 9}+6+5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{8}-3+6+5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{19-3}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 16=0 \end{aligned}\) Option 4),\(-,+, \div,+\) Mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right: \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 8-27+9 \div 6+5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{8}-27+1.5+5=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \underline{14.5-27}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-12.5=0 \end{aligned}\) Hence, the correct answer is ",\(+, \div,-,-\) ".
